caveat: Measured in-process against the vscode stub. These are the EXTENSION'S OWN synchronous costs on the host side — real. They EXCLUDE extension-host startup overhead and all renderer-side work (webview process spawn, HTML/CSS parse, script evaluation, first paint), which a Node harness cannot reach. Layer 3 owns first paint in S4, against both implementations.

activateMs.covers: extension activate(): provider construction, command registration, watchers, context keys

resolveWebviewViewMs.covers: host half of showing the view: HTML assembly, message wiring, options. A TreeDataProvider removes this entirely.

webviewPayloadBytes.covers: what the renderer must fetch/parse/execute before first paint. Reported as BYTES, not ms, because timing it needs a renderer. This is the bucket the migration deletes outright.
